questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: It was crucial to me that the university had courses in the subjects, I found interesting. Furthermore, new cultures (both University-culture and people-culture), level of education, and future career possibilities were a part of my motivation.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: You have to take time off to navigate in the documents you receive from both host and home university. However, the information was always there. You just had to find it.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: The University was open so it was possible to go there and ask any questions. The most assistance, I got, was from fellow students in the same situation as me. This helped a lot and it was easy to find helpful friends in the beginning.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I applied through the host institution and they offered me accomodation. I did not have an influence on the location. I would recommend to do the same. However, do not expect a lot. It is not pure luxary and it is mostly dorms where you will share kitchen and bathroom with other students.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: As mentioned above: it is fine for one semester but do not expect to live in luxary if you apply through the university.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: It is not that different from University of Copenhagen. You apply for courses through a webpage.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Information emails from the university.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got what I wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: In the beginning, I would apply for all courses, I find interesting. It is possible to deregister later.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: ETH is a lot of work. The facilities are great. The level is high but the level of teaching is not much higher than University of Copenhagen.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level was much higher than University of Copenhagen. The workload was the double.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Lab courses was great. Semester courses were just lectures and then a lot of selfstudying before the exams.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Plant Biochemistry
Phytopathology
Concepts in modern genetics
Molecular life of plants
Cellular biochemistry
Microbiology (Part I)

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: The block courses Plant biochemistry and phytopathology. The rest was all good. However, I would not recommend to have too many exams in the end (four were too many for me).

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Switxerland is expensive. Expect to use a lot of money on everything. I went hiking and skiing - this was only possible because of grants and scholarship.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Everything was more expensive.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Great sports facilities.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Not much because of corona. A lot of sports were offered for free at the university.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Hiking, skiing, all kinds of sports.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Grindelwald, Zermatt (Matterhorn), skiing in Crans Montana was good and cheaper than St. Moritz/Davos.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy. It is a european country and most people are good at english.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Do the intensive German course in the beginning of the semester.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The work ethics and the expectations to students.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The great hiking culture.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Avoid having too many exams.
2. Do block courses if possible for your study direction.
3. Expect a huge workload.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Apply for grants.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Meeting new people and the nature.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The workload and the dorm, where I was living, was not as cozy as my home dorm.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
